trigger4_delta.finding: F2-WP-005 telemetry initializer has bounded repository runtime evidence, but reusable structured emitters/collectors, run finalization/source-completeness, internal latency/resource collectors and integrated coverage remain open.

trigger5_delta.finding: Effect/completion evidence must bind immutable invocation/effect/generation identities and fail closed on failed, denied, unchecked, unbound or unknown outcomes. Observation cannot become effect authority.

trigger6_control_delta.finding: Private clay-global-research-entity GitHub Actions currently exhibit a zero-step pre-admission blocker. This is transport/admission evidence, not a semantic negative for the Trigger6 SQLite materializer. Trigger6 seeds remain pending/nonpromoting.

conflicts: AgentSight has its own SQLite session storage; F2 UnifiedDB must remain canonical and any AgentSight DB must be witness/derived evidence only.
AgentSight raw events are process/time/source centric and do not natively carry F2 causal_event_id, invocation_id, generation or EffectJournal identity.
Kernel/TLS observation can strengthen effect evidence but cannot establish that an F2 effect was authorized, semantically correct or externally complete.
unresolved_gaps: No exact F2 ablation has measured AgentSight coverage, overhead, event loss, timestamp skew, duplicate rate or secret exposure.
No mapping is yet accepted from AgentSight event rows into F2 typed telemetry envelopes.
No E3 source/runtime reproduction has been executed by this Trigger6 worker.

source_audit.observed_architecture: eBPF programs -> JSON event stream -> native capture core -> analyzer chain/materialized view -> SQLite/OTel/CLI/web sinks, with agent-native session sources as a non-eBPF path.
observed_capture_surfaces: SSL/TLS plaintext at instrumented library boundaries where supported
agent-native session files and saved SQLite sessions

raw_event_core.f2_implication: Useful as an external witness envelope, but insufficient as canonical F2 causal identity. F2 must add/bind causal_event_id, invocation_id, generation, source identity, admission identity and EffectJournal/effect receipt identity.

operational_boundaries: eBPF-backed capture is Linux-specific and requires elevated BPF privileges; portable report/native-session paths can work without eBPF.
Static BoringSSL/OpenSSL binaries require binary discovery or explicit target binding; thread/process naming can break naive comm filters.
Electron/IDE agents can be outside the eBPF/TLS capture path; some use protobuf payloads that do not yield recognized LLM events.
Captured data can include prompts, responses, headers, paths and network targets and therefore is security/privacy sensitive.

upstream_evaluation_claim.paper: AgentSight: System-Level Observability for AI Agents Using eBPF, arXiv:2508.02736
upstream_evaluation_claim.claim: Authors report less than 3% overhead in their evaluated workloads and demonstrate prompt-injection, reasoning-loop and multi-agent bottleneck detection.

hypothesis: A bounded AgentSight-derived witness adapter can materially improve F2 telemetry coverage and root-cause closure for child processes, file/network effects, tool/model activity and resource use without modifying F2 agent code.
counterhypotheses: F2-native telemetry may already cover the useful signals with lower privilege, lower sensitivity and cleaner causal identity.
TLS/eBPF capture fragility across runtimes may make evidence coverage nonuniform and version-sensitive.
An extra observer may increase overhead, duplicate events or leak sensitive payloads without improving causal discrimination.
AgentSight correlation may look causal while still lacking F2's immutable invocation/effect/generation identity.

integration_design.authority_boundary: AgentSight emits witness observations only. It may corroborate or contradict F2 telemetry and EffectJournal receipts, but cannot mint canonical state, authorize effects, close workpackages or turn UNKNOWN outcomes into success.
integration_design.storage_boundary: AgentSight SQLite remains ephemeral/derived witness storage. Canonical admitted evidence is normalized through F2 typed telemetry/UnifiedDB with provenance to the exact AgentSight source/version/session artifact.
minimum_adapter_fields: F2 invocation/effect/generation binding when deterministically resolvable

trigger4_discriminator.goal: Determine whether AgentSight provides independent evidence gain worth its privilege/overhead/sensitivity cost.
arms: B: F2 telemetry + AgentSight native-session/process-snapshot path where available without eBPF
C: F2 telemetry + AgentSight eBPF/TLS witness on an admitted isolated Linux test surface
required_measurements: false-positive and false-negative witness rate against deterministic fixtures
CPU, RSS and wall-time overhead with p50/p95/p99
failure behavior for static SSL, unsupported IDE/protobuf and no-privilege paths
fail_closed_tests: AgentSight-only observation cannot satisfy F2 completion.
AgentSight-only observation cannot authorize an effect.
Unbound pid/timestamp similarity cannot be promoted to exact invocation identity.
Redaction failure or ambiguous provenance blocks canonical admission of captured payload fields.
Observer disagreement preserves UNKNOWN/CONFLICT rather than selecting the convenient source.
trigger4_discriminator.promotion_rule: Only a Trigger4 exact-source measured ablation may promote this research beyond E2. E5 requires a reproducible handoff with baseline, measurement receipts and exact source pins; E6 requires actual F2 acceptance evidence.

result.next_exact_action: Trigger4 should implement the smallest noncanonical AgentSight witness adapter behind the existing telemetry spine and run the A/B/C ablation above on exact admitted source identity. If the no-eBPF arm yields most of the independent evidence, prefer it over privileged capture.
